lessons.title: Mergers, Acquisitions, and Demergers: What Actually Happens to the Company

children.text: In July 2023, two groups of Indian investors opened their Zerodha holdings and saw something they had not bought. Shareholders of HDFC Ltd found that stock gone, replaced by HDFC Bank shares. Shareholders of Reliance Industries found a brand new line in their demat account: Jio Financial Services. Nobody placed an order. Both changes came from corporate deals approved months earlier, and both were entirely predictable to anyone who had read the announcements.

body.text: Every deal headline raises two separate questions: what happens to the company, and what happens to your shares. Mergers, acquisitions and demergers answer both questions differently. Know which deal you are looking at and you know what to expect in your demat account.

children.text: Three Deals, Three Different Outcomes

People say "M&A" as if it were one thing. For an investor, it is at least three, and they move in opposite directions. A merger combines two companies into one. An acquisition hands control of one company to another while both can keep existing. A demerger splits one company into two.

body.caption: The three deal types at a glance

cells: Two companies become one. The company being absorbed ceases to exist.
If you held the absorbed company, your shares are cancelled and replaced with shares of the surviving company at a fixed swap ratio.
HDFC Ltd into HDFC Bank, effective 1 July 2023
One company buys control of another. The target usually survives, often as a subsidiary.
Nothing changes automatically. If the target is listed, you may get an open offer to sell your shares to the buyer.
One company carves out a business into a separate company.
You keep your original shares and also receive shares of the new company in a fixed ratio.
Jio Financial Services from Reliance Industries, 2023

children.text: Mergers: Two Become One
In a merger, one company (the
transferor company
) hands all its assets, liabilities, employees and contracts to another (the
transferee company
), and then dissolves without being wound up. Indian law calls this an amalgamation, and it runs through a
scheme of arrangement
under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013. The transferor's shareholders are not paid in cash. They receive shares of the transferee in a pre-agreed
swap ratio

markDefs.definition: The company that is absorbed in a merger and ceases to exist once the scheme takes effect.
The surviving company in a merger, which takes over the business of the transferor and issues shares to its shareholders.
A court-style restructuring plan for mergers, demergers and similar reorganisations. It needs board, shareholder, creditor, stock exchange and NCLT approval. Lesson 2.1 walks through each step.
The number of shares of the surviving company you receive for each share of the absorbed company. Lesson 2.2 covers how it is set.

body.label: HDFC Ltd and HDFC Bank merger swap ratio
body.value: 42 HDFC Bank shares for every 25 HDFC Ltd shares
body.context: Announced in April 2022 and effective 1 July 2023. HDFC Ltd was delisted, and its former shareholders ended up owning about 41% of the combined HDFC Bank.

body.latex: \text{New shares received} = \text{Shares held in absorbed company} \times \frac{42}{25}
body.caption: The HDFC swap ratio applied to any holding. Every merger has its own ratio, fixed in the scheme.

body.title: Convert an HDFC Ltd holding
body.prompt: Priya held 150 shares of HDFC Ltd on the record date. Using the swap ratio of 42 HDFC Bank shares for every 25 HDFC Ltd shares, how many HDFC Bank shares did she receive?
body.explanation: 150 × 42 ÷ 25 = 6,300 ÷ 25 = 252 HDFC Bank shares. Her 150 HDFC Ltd shares were extinguished at the same time.

body.title: Who owned HDFC Bank after the merger (approximate)

body.text: A merger never creates value on the day your shares convert. Your HDFC Ltd stake became a smaller slice of a much bigger bank. Whether you gained depends on whether the combined business earns more than the two would have earned apart, and that plays out over years, not on the record date.

body.title: What if the swap ratio gives you a fraction of a share?

children.text: Had Priya held 60 HDFC Ltd shares, the maths gives 60 × 42 ÷ 25 = 100.8 shares. Companies cannot issue 0.8 of a share, so she would get 100 shares directly. Schemes usually pool every shareholder's fractional entitlements, allot the resulting whole shares to a trustee, sell them in the market and pay each shareholder their share of the sale proceeds in cash. Check the scheme document for the exact treatment, because the cash for a fraction is a sale and has tax consequences, covered in Lesson 5.1.
Acquisitions: One Buys Control of Another

An acquisition is about control, not combination. The buyer pays for a controlling stake with cash, its own shares or both, and the target usually carries on as a separate company. What you experience depends on which side of the deal you hold.
You hold the buyer.

Your share count stays the same, but the company's balance sheet changes. In June 2022, Zomato (now Eternal) agreed to buy quick-commerce startup Blinkit for about ₹4,447 crore, paid entirely in newly issued Zomato shares. Zomato shareholders owned a slightly smaller percentage of a company that now also owned Blinkit. Blinkit, being unlisted, simply became a wholly owned subsidiary.
You hold the target.

The target stays listed and your shares stay in your demat account, but you now have a new controlling shareholder. In 2022, the Adani Group indirectly acquired a 29.18% stake in NDTV by taking over RRPR Holding, a promoter entity. Crossing 25% triggered SEBI's
open offer
requirement, so NDTV's public shareholders were offered the chance to sell up to another 26% of the company to the acquirer.

markDefs.definition: An offer an acquirer must make to a listed company's public shareholders to buy their shares, required under SEBI's Takeover Regulations once certain ownership or control thresholds are crossed. Lesson 2.3 covers the rules.

columns.label: Merger
points: Absorbed company is dissolved and delisted
Shareholders are paid in shares at a swap ratio
Needs a scheme approved by shareholders and NCLT
Your old shares are replaced automatically

columns.label: Acquisition
points: Both companies can continue to exist
Target often stays listed as a subsidiary
Buyer pays cash, shares or a mix for a controlling stake
Often done through a share purchase, triggering an open offer if listed
Nothing happens to your shares unless you choose to tender

body.text: Headlines blur these words constantly. Deals are routinely called "mergers" when one side is clearly buying the other. Ignore the headline word and read the exchange filing: are shares being swapped under a scheme, or is a stake being bought for cash? That tells you what will actually happen to your holding.

children.text: Demergers: One Becomes Two
A demerger runs a merger in reverse. The
demerged company
transfers one of its businesses into a
resulting company
, and the parent's shareholders receive shares of the resulting company in proportion to what they already hold. You end up owning the same businesses as before, now split across two listed stocks.

markDefs.definition: The parent company that transfers one of its businesses out in a demerger. It continues to exist and stay listed.
The company that receives the demerged business and issues its shares to the parent's shareholders.

body.title: How Jio Financial Services was demerged from Reliance

events.title: Demerger takes effect
events.description: After NCLT approval, Reliance's financial services business formally moves into Jio Financial Services. The ratio: 1 JFS share for every 1 Reliance share held.

events.title: Record date and price discovery
events.description: Shareholders on the register this day are entitled to JFS shares. A special pre-open session on NSE and BSE sets the value to be carved out of Reliance's share price, discovering JFS at ₹261.85 per share.

events.title: JFS lists on NSE and BSE
events.description: JFS lists at ₹265 on BSE and hits its 5% lower circuit on day one. Shareholders could not sell their JFS shares during the month between the record date and listing.

children.text: Ratios are not always one for one. ITC demerged its hotels business into ITC Hotels with effect from 1 January 2025, giving shareholders 1 ITC Hotels share for every 10 ITC shares. Unlike Reliance, ITC kept a large stake in the new company for itself.

stats.label: Entitlement ratio
stats.context: 1 ITC Hotels share per 10 ITC shares

stats.label: Held by ITC's shareholders
stats.context: In proportion to their ITC holding

body.title: Your ITC Hotels entitlement
body.prompt: Arvind held 250 ITC shares on the record date of 6 January 2025. How many ITC Hotels shares did he receive?
body.explanation: 250 ÷ 10 × 1 = 25 ITC Hotels shares. Arvind still holds all 250 ITC shares. Unlike a merger, nothing is cancelled in a demerger; he simply owns the hotels business through a separate stock now.

body.text: On the record date, the parent's share price drops by roughly the value carved out. That fall is not a loss. The value has moved into the new shares heading to your account. Judge your position by adding both holdings together, not by staring at the parent's price alone.

body.title: Name the deal
body.question: A fictional filing reads: "The Board of Narmada Industries Ltd has approved a scheme to transfer its specialty chemicals business into Narmada Chemicals Ltd. Shareholders of Narmada Industries will receive 1 share of Narmada Chemicals for every 4 shares held. Both companies will be listed." What kind of deal is this?
options: A merger, because two companies are named in a scheme
An acquisition, because Narmada Chemicals is buying a business
A demerger, because one company is splitting a business out and shareholders receive shares of the new entity
An open offer, because shareholders are receiving new shares
body.explanation: A business moves out of the parent into a separate company, the parent survives, and existing shareholders receive shares of the new company in a fixed ratio. That is a demerger. Narmada Industries is the demerged company and Narmada Chemicals is the resulting company.

body.title: Get the vocabulary right
body.textWithBlank: In a demerger, the parent's shareholders receive shares of the ___ company.
body.explanation: The company that receives the carved-out business is the resulting company. The parent that gives up the business is the demerged company. You will see both terms in every Indian demerger scheme and tax rule.

children.text: Reading a Deal Headline About a Stock You Own

body.title: The demerger announcement
body.scenario: Rohan holds 400 shares of Narmada Industries, the fictional company from the quiz. He bought it mainly because he likes its specialty chemicals business. The morning after the demerger announcement, the stock is up 6% and a WhatsApp group is calling it "free shares".
body.prompt: What will Rohan actually receive, and what should he check before reacting?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Entitlement: 400 ÷ 4 = 100 Narmada Chemicals shares, and he keeps all 400 Narmada Industries shares.
2. Nothing is free. The chemicals business already belongs to him through the parent. On the record date, the parent's price will fall by roughly the value carved out.
3. Timeline: the scheme still needs shareholder, stock exchange and NCLT approval. That often takes a year or more, and the new shares can take weeks after the record date to list.
4. Where his thesis lives: the business he likes is moving to the resulting company. He should look at what stays behind in the parent and decide whether he still wants to own that part.
5. Paperwork: after the demerger, his original purchase cost will be split between the two holdings. Lesson 4.3 shows how, and it matters when he eventually sells either one.

body.title: Two dates in every scheme: appointed date vs effective date

children.text: Appointed date.
The date from which the merger or demerger is treated as having happened for accounting purposes. It is often set in the past, such as the start of a financial year.
Effective date.
The date the scheme legally comes into force, once the NCLT order is filed with the Registrar of Companies and every condition is met.
For your demat account, neither date is the one that matters most. The record date decides who gets the new shares, and the listing date decides when you can sell them.

body.title: When a deal headline hits a stock you own
steps: Open the company's announcement on the BSE or NSE website instead of relying on news headlines
Identify the deal type: merger, acquisition or demerger
Find the swap ratio, entitlement ratio or open offer price
Note which side you hold: absorbed company, surviving company, buyer, target, parent or resulting company
List the approvals still pending and expect the process to take months
Check where the business you originally invested in will sit after the deal

body.label: BSE Corporate Announcements
body.description: Search any listed company to read its board outcomes, schemes of arrangement and record date notices at the source. Lesson 5.2 shows how to track deals here and on screener.in.

cards.definition: Two companies combine into one. The absorbed company dissolves and its shareholders receive shares of the surviving company.
One company buys a controlling stake in another. The target usually continues to exist, often as a subsidiary.
A company transfers one of its businesses into a separate company, whose shares go to the parent's shareholders.
The number of surviving company shares issued for each share of the absorbed company in a merger.
The legal route for mergers and demergers under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, approved by shareholders, creditors and the NCLT.
An offer by an acquirer to buy shares from a listed target's public shareholders, triggered under SEBI's Takeover Regulations.
The company that receives the carved-out business in a demerger.
The date that decides which shareholders are entitled to new shares from a merger or demerger.

points: A merger turns two companies into one: HDFC Ltd shareholders received 42 HDFC Bank shares for every 25 they held, and HDFC Ltd ceased to exist.
An acquisition transfers control but both companies can survive. Target shareholders may get an open offer, but nothing happens to their shares automatically.
A demerger turns one company into two: Reliance shareholders kept their shares and received 1 Jio Financial Services share for each Reliance share.
No deal creates value on the day your shares convert or arrive. Value comes from what the businesses earn afterwards.
Read the exchange filing, not the headline, to learn the ratio, the record date and which side of the deal you hold.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment, tax or legal advice. Narmada Industries, Narmada Chemicals and the investors in the examples are fictional. Figures for real companies are taken from public disclosures at the time of each deal and are rounded where noted. Always read the actual scheme document and exchange filings before acting on any corporate action.
